page_title: How to spend your first 30 days in a new senior-level role

summary.title: How to spend your first 30 days in a new senior-level role
summary.one_liner: Learn why a new leader should spend their first 30 days listening, how to run listening-tour one-on-ones, and how to close the period by sharing themes with the organization before making changes.
keywords: first 30 days in a new role
building trust as a new director
how to introduce change as a new leader
all hands recap for new leader
when new leaders should avoid changes
takeaways: Spend the first 30 days in listen-only mode, avoiding changes to processes, meetings, or roadmaps unless someone's health or safety is at risk.
Schedule 30-minute one-on-ones with the whole team, cross-functional peers, and stakeholders, asking what should change and what is working well.
Use follow-up questions such as the risk of not changing and who else to talk to, reflecting back what you hear.
At the end of 30 days, synthesize one or two future-focused themes and share them at an all hands, avoiding specific past examples.
State clear, followable communication channels and cadences going forward, and avoid rescheduling commitments.
summary.summary: Lara Hogan, a leadership coach, explains how someone starting a director-or-above role should use their first 30 days as a listening period she calls "sponge mode." The article gives the reasoning for avoiding early changes, a template for invitations, and a step-by-step script for one-on-ones with two core questions and follow-ups. It then covers how to synthesize themes at the end of the month, present them at an all hands to help people feel heard, and set clear communication expectations. It is a short opinion and advice piece with no tools or code.
